answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using hardware enclave attestation bound to a unique processor die. To join a trading haven, an agent binds an ephemeral key inside a CPU enclave and returns a vendor-signed quote within a strict challenge-response delta. Since the registry permits one active key per silicon ID, attackers cannot clone identities in an umber server without buying separate physical chips. However, side-channel leaks or bulk bare-metal rentals still limit exclusivity.
